title: Useful alerts: symptom rather than cause, noise and on-call fatigue

videos.script: An alert is a decision to interrupt a person. At three in the morning, that person is asleep, and the alert has to be worth it. {{interrupt}} This lesson writes the shop's alerts again, from the objective of lesson 15 instead of from its causes. The question stops being is payments failing, and becomes are customers losing checkouts fast enough to matter. {{symptom}} A burn rate answers that, measured over two windows at once. A short blip does not page anybody. {{blip}} A real failure does, within minutes. {{incident}} Then the alert has to reach the right place. Pages go to the pager, tickets wait for the morning, and a page about checkouts silences the ticket about the same thing. {{routes}} You silence it during maintenance, with a reason somebody can read later. {{silence}} And you look at how a team drowns in alerts that nobody acts on, and what to do about it. {{fatigue}}
